summary: Tested the Membrane voice (Evan) and the change that gives each sentence the earlier text of the same reply as context. Backend: 4/4 pytest pass, using 3 real ElevenLabs calls plus 1 validation call that ElevenLabs never sees. Frontend: as a signed-out visitor on /presence/membrane with voice ON, sent one message. All 4 TTS checks pass, the full reply shows on screen, and the page made exactly one /api/membrane/start.

issues: Labels read 'HER VOICE' / 'HER POSTURE' while the new voice is Evan (likely a male voice). Check config.gender for membrane if this matters to David. Cosmetic, not in scope.

backend: POST /api/tts/speak {text, presence:'membrane'}: 200, voice_id TWutjvRaJqAX89preB4e, format mp3, base64 audio >1KB
frontend_reply_tts_requests: Reply (317 chars on screen, 4 sentences) produced 4 /api/tts/speak calls, all 200, all presence='membrane'
#0: 75 chars ('The room is a place where you're already welcome before you've said a word.'), so >=60; previous_text absent
#1-#3: each previous_text is exactly the earlier sentences of this reply, joined in order (cumulative). The last piece (32 chars) still gets context
Welcome message TTS (spoken through speak(), not the stream) was blocked in the test to save quota and is not part of the reply checks
regression: Full reply text rendered in msg-assistant; thread status stays THREAD OPEN; welcome plus user plus reply stay in one thread

The first browser run counted 2 /start requests because the test tool loads the URL and then the script loads it again. Backend logs show only one /api/membrane/start for that run. A clean single-load probe confirmed exactly 1 /start.

critical_code_review_comments: usePresenceVoice.speak() (used for non-streamed messages such as the /start welcome) still synthesizes stage-direction-split segments in parallel with no previous_text and no 60-char first-piece merge. A welcome like '*settles* I'm here.' can still sound cold. Consider passing previous_text between segments there too (they would then need to run one after another).

extractSentences minLen counts raw piece length, including *stage directions* that cleanTextForSpeech does NOT strip (only the backend strips them). For example, '*settles* Hi.' passes 60 chars more easily than its spoken text would. Minor.
The backend truncates previous_text to the last 400 chars, while Pydantic allows up to 1000. Consistent with the frontend; fine.
seed_data_creation: None. 2 ephemeral membrane sessions were created by the chamber visits (listed above). Nothing was deleted.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_tts_previous_text.py makes 3 real ElevenLabs calls. When intercepting chamber TTS, abort the /api/tts/speak calls made before sending (the welcome) to save quota. The browser_automation tool loads page_url before the script runs: don't page.goto the same URL again, or /start gets counted twice.
